title: The Android project: modules, manifest, Gradle and resources

videos.script: This course builds one app, a study planner, and it starts today with eight files and one sentence on a screen. {{boundary}} First, the honest part. Almost everything here runs on your computer, with no phone. Building, testing, even screenshots. Running the app on a device is the part that needs one, and you will know now which lessons that touches. {{sdk}} Then the SDK. One zip from Google, two lines in your shell's start-up file, and a new tool called android that installs the rest. {{fails}} Then the three ways that goes wrong, each with a message that names its own cause. {{project}} Then the project, written by hand: the settings, a catalogue of every version this course uses, a build file, a manifest, one string and one activity. {{build}} One command turns them into an APK. The first time takes minutes, the second takes seconds, and you will see why. {{apk}} And then you open the APK, because it is a zip file. Five files of code, and nearly none of it yours.
